nodes.title: Amit Jhingran
nodes.summary: In this MD & CEO message, Amit Jhingran highlights SBI Life's standout FY25 performance, including 12.3% growth in Individual Rated Premium (IRP) versus the industry's 10.5%, and discusses life insurance at a crossroads with low penetration in India despite regulatory support. He covers adapting to evolving customer needs through 13 new and 20 re-launched products, maintaining a low ULIP surrender ratio of 6.23% and improved persistency (87.41% 13th month, 62.69% 61st month). Digital innovation is emphasized with 98.7% of individual proposals submitted digitally, 54% automated underwriting, and AI tools like InsightGenie and chatbot Ria. Scaling to serve India better includes a 70-branch expansion, 15% agency productivity increase, 61% bancassurance contribution, and over 162k policies via SBI's YONO. Delivering performance reflects purpose: 2.2 million new policies, 12.6 million in-force base, 43% growth in new business sum assured to ₹2,769 billion, 99.40% death claim settlement ratio, gross written premium of ₹849.8 billion, and a 3-year CAGR of 15%. Profitable growth with a strong financial foundation is shown through profit after tax of ₹24.1 billion (+27%), operating expense ratio 5.3%, total cost ratio 9.7%, AUM ₹4.5 trillion (+15%), solvency ratio 1.96, VoNB ₹59.5 billion with 27.8% margin, embedded value ₹702.5 billion (+21%), and a dividend of ₹2.70/share. Growing responsibly and sustainably covers ESG priorities, renewable energy, energy efficiency, digital servicing, 23% gender diversity, and ₹182 million CSR impacting over 53,000 lives. Shaping tomorrow: regulatory and market outlook notes alignment with IRDAI reforms and projects India's market growth at 6.9% from 2025-2029 vs global 3%, with global premiums reaching USD 4.8 trillion by 2035. Supporting the dreams of every Indian outlines strategic pillars (Agency 2.0, digital acceleration, rural outreach, insight-led simplicity) and thanks stakeholders, looking forward to the 25th year.

nodes.title: B. Development
nodes.summary: The life insurance distribution landscape has shifted from agent-driven to diversified channels including bancassurance, digital, and direct sales. Multi-channel and digital hybrid models are expected to gain traction, especially among urban and younger customers, with digital adoption accelerating post-COVID for term and savings plans. The product mix includes protection, savings/investment-linked, pension, group, and specialized products, with traditional products dominating due to their guaranteed savings and fixed returns appeal. Private insurers have a higher share of ULIPs, positioned as transparent, flexible investment solutions. Tax changes under the Finance Act 2021 and 2023, and Union Budget 2025, subject high-premium ULIPs and non-ULIP policies to capital gains tax, necessitating tax planning and product redesign for tax efficiency.
